title: Rules and expectations the business owns
sub: Business architecture for data, the second series on enterprise architecture: where the business's rules come from, a policy carried out by processes, procedures and records; a decision's rules kept in a table beside the step that applies them; quality expectations set by the owner of the step that uses the data, written down before any check is built; the source checking its own data first; and the data product whose contract holds what its readers expect.
howto: Glass in the layers' colours is the confirmed model: yellow is the business layer, where the processes sit, salmon the information layer, where the business's concepts sit, and purple a requirement, a rule or an expectation. Gold marks an owner; blue the data team. Amber marks an estimate, and a reading late for the step that needs it. In the desert, blue is the water, and the people of the story are silhouettes.
